symptoms: Small reddish-brown to gray spots on the upper leaf surface
Lesions may enlarge and develop pale centers with dark margins
Premature yellowing and leaf drop under severe infection
recommendedActions: Remove heavily infected plant debris after harvest and avoid carrying residue between fields.
Use certified, disease-free soybean seed and follow locally approved seed treatment guidance.
Apply a registered fungicide only when disease pressure and local agricultural guidance justify treatment.
prevention: Rotate soybean with non-legume crops for at least one season.
Maintain recommended plant spacing and avoid excessive canopy humidity.
Choose locally recommended tolerant soybean varieties.
diseaseDetections.explanation: Soybean leaf spot is a fungal disease that can reduce photosynthetic leaf area. Accurate confirmation requires a close, well-lit image of the affected soybean leaf.

symptoms: Concentric dark brown rings forming target-like patterns on older leaves
Yellowing (chlorosis) surrounding necrotic lesions
Premature defoliation starting from the lower canopy upward
Sunscald on exposed developing fruit due to leaf loss
recommendedActions: Immediately prune and destroy severely infected lower leaves; do not compost infected foliage.
Apply copper hydroxide or Mancozeb (2-2.5g/L water) strictly in accordance with local CIBRC safety guidelines.
Ensure soil-directed irrigation; avoid overhead sprinkler watering that wets leaves.
Maintain 24-48 hour observation window before secondary foliar application.
prevention: Practice 3-year crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops (e.g., maize, pulses).
Use certified pathogen-free seeds and blight-resistant hybrids.
Apply organic mulch (paddy straw) around plants to prevent soil splash during rain.
diseaseDetections.explanation: Early blight is caused by the fungal pathogen Alternaria solani, favored by warm temperatures (24-29°C) and alternating wet-and-dry periods.

symptoms: Linear stripes of bright yellow powdery pustules (uredinia) along leaf veins
Chlorotic stripes that eventually turn necrotic and cause premature senescence
Reduced grain weight, shriveled kernels, and stunted wheat stalks
recommendedActions: Spray Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1ml/L or Tebuconazole @ 1ml/L immediately upon detection of the first stripe.
Ensure uniform foliar coverage using 200 liters of spray solution per acre.
Inspect adjacent wheat plots within 1 km perimeter.
prevention: Cultivate rust-resistant varieties approved by ICAR-IIWBR.
Avoid early sowing in northern hill and sub-mountainous zones.
diseaseDetections.explanation: Stripe rust spreads via long-distance windborne spores under cool, humid conditions (10-15°C) common in northern winter plains.

symptoms: Concentric dark brown rings forming target-like patterns on older leaves

recommendedActions: Immediately prune and destroy severely infected lower leaves.

Suspend overhead sprinkler watering.
prevention: Apply organic straw mulch to prevent soil splash during rain.
diseaseDetections.explanation: Early blight caused by Alternaria solani was identified with 94% confidence, triggered by recent warm humid weather.

symptoms: Upward curling, puckering, and reduction of leaf size
Bushy stunted plant growth with poor fruit set
recommendedActions: Vector control: spray Diafenthiuron @ 1g/L for whitefly control.
Uproot and bury severely infected plants.
Install yellow sticky traps across the plot.
prevention: Plant border barrier rows of maize or sorghum.
